question: Can a single review predict an unseen author's independently measured genre preference?
status_at_registration: No predictive model results have been computed for this protocol.

data.primary: Existing development sample, one review per author, only single preferences retained after removing the entire input-book history from preference evidence
data.outer_primary: 3 book-disjoint folds using SHA256 of book identifier
data.inner: One deterministic book-disjoint approximately 20% holdout within each outer training fold
data.common_input_genre: Train on existing development Romance/Science Fiction authors' thriller reviews, evaluate on separate existing validation authors' thriller reviews; remove training titles and exact normalized bodies seen in evaluation
data.final_test: Not opened. Existing validation has already been used in EDA and is not a pristine final test.

models.style: All 29 frozen metrics, log1p, training median imputation, training IQR or SD scaling, clip to [-5,5], divide by sqrt(29)
models.words: Existing fixed tokenizer, unigrams and bigrams, training-only DF >=5 and <=65%, maximum 12000 terms, log TF and smoothed IDF, unit row norm. No SVD.
models.context: Diagnostic only: book genre indicators, log review token count and its square; no rating, identity, or preference history is an input
models.selection: Inner macro-F1, choose stronger regularization on ties
models.secondary_algorithm: Multinomial naive Bayes on lexical counts, Laplace smoothing 1, empirical class priors
baselines: random training class frequencies with fixed random settings
models.all_preprocessing: Refit separately on inner training and outer training; no existing full-development TFIDF fit is reused

secondary: six adequately represented genres, described separately
evaluation.uncertainty: 2000 paired bootstrap resamples of book titles, holding out-of-fold predictions fixed; model-training uncertainty is not fully represented
evaluation.practical_threshold_status: Analyst-chosen feasibility criteria, not universal statistical standards or a user-specified deployment requirement
evaluation.main_gate: Book-disjoint combined macro-F1 >=0.40 AND balanced accuracy >=0.40 AND >=0.05 absolute improvement over both baselines for both metrics AND paired 95% lower bounds above zero
evaluation.context_gate: Context plus combined features improves on context alone by >=0.05 in both metrics AND paired 95% lower bounds above zero
evaluation.common_genre_gate: Combined features improve on majority AND length-only logistic baseline by >=0.05 in both metrics with paired 95% lower bounds above zero in the separate-author/title common-genre comparison
evaluation.continue: Main gate AND (context gate OR common-genre gate). This is evidence to continue within represented genres, not a deployment claim.
evaluation.underrepresented_genre: Fewer than 50 independently labelled authors precludes a positive adequacy claim for that genre
evaluation.negative: If continuation gate is not met, do not commit to full preference prediction phases; assess a replacement objective. This does not prove all language representations or all populations lack an association.
evaluation.no_result_chasing: No adding vocabulary filters, embeddings, regularization options, labels or thresholds in response to predictive outcomes within this experiment
